events.title: English Language Learners' (ELL) Conversation Club (via Pearl and Cambrian)
events.description: San Jose Public Library presents an English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club that creates a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English conversation skills. Club meetings will convene weekly with an online meeting with our Pearl Avenue librarians and an ELL facilitator, on Tuesdays, 11:00 a.m. - 12:00 pm. Test your English skills with others who are learning English, too. Everyone is welcome! Please register by clicking on the Register button. When you give us your email, we are able to send you a link to the Zoom meeting, on the day of the program. Usually, the links will arrive about 30 minutes before the class begins.
events.blurb: Practice everyday English conversation with fellow adult learners in a relaxed weekly session at the library.

events.title: Landscape Design for Beginners
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Discover the fundamentals of landscape design in this beginner-friendly class. Learn essential design principles, how to use plant size and spacing to create balanced garden spaces, and techniques for adding eye-catching focal points. Apply what you learn in two hands-on activities featuring California native and other water-wise plants. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn basic landscape design principles, including plant spacing and layout, in this beginner class.

events.title: Ukulele Jam Sing and Play Along
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Would you like to learn some fun songs on the ukulele? Beginners and ukulele enthusiasts are welcome to join us to sing and play together. Ukulele instructor Chuck Monahan will teach participants how to play basic chords on the ukulele and lead the group in an informal performance of popular songs from the last 50 years. Bring your own uke, or use one of ours. Ages 12 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Sing and strum along with ukulele instructor Chuck Monahan in a beginner-friendly play-along session.

events.title: Sci-Fi Trivia Night
events.description: Registration is required and seats are limited. This event is intended for adults, ages 18 and up only. Join us to test your knowledge on all things sci-fi and fantasy related! In teams of 5, you will work together to answer 40 questions from 4 sci-fi related categories. Fly solo or come with your friends, the top 3 teams will take home a prize. If you come in sci-fi/fantasy costume, your team will receive 2 bonus points! Light refreshments and snacks will be provided. A Sci-Fi September Event This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Team up with four others to answer 40 sci-fi and fantasy trivia questions across categories.

events.title: Mid-Autumn Festival Story Celebration
events.description: Celebrate the magic of the Mid-Autumn Festival with Piggy Sprout! Join Tianxin (Aries) Wang for immersive Mandarin stories that bring the rich traditions of Asian culture to life. Drawing upon her advanced academic background in language acquisition, Aries curates an interactive experience featuring beautifully illustrated picture books, cultural connection, and engaging hands-on activities. This session is thoughtfully designed to foster early language development while helping children build a joyful, lasting connection to their cultural roots. Whether you are seeking to strengthen your family's heritage or introduce your child to a new language in a welcoming community space, this festive gathering promises a memorable and educational experience.
events.blurb: Hear Mandarin storytelling from Tianxin Wang celebrating Mid-Autumn Festival traditions and Asian culture.

events.title: Sci-Fi Fur-endship Charm Workshop
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Do you think Dungeon Crawler Carl and Princess Donut would wear matching charms? We think yes! Channel your inner crawler and craft like your life depends on it! In this workshop you will have the chance to customize a charm bracelet and along with your cat's collar. Bring in your collar from home or choose one of the collars available day of. You will be able to select from a variety of sci-fi themed charms. If you don't have a cat, no problem, anyone will be able to create a charm bracelet. This class is intended for ages 18 and up only. A Sci-Fi September Event This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Craft a Dungeon Crawler Carl-inspired charm in this sci-fi themed hands-on workshop.

events.title: Dogbotic Build a Synth
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Ever wanted to build a synthesizer? In this beginners workshop led by Dogbotic, participants will learn the process step-by-step, demystifying the horrible world of electrical engineering at every turn. You'll learn how to build basic oscillators, filters, LFOs, and amplifiers, how to rig up your circuit to be light-sensitive, and oh-so-much more. Each participant will make their own working synth prototype, which well tune together to form a delicious sound bath. You'll then get to take your prototype home and use it to impress and irritate your friends and loved ones. All parts are included, no prior circuitry experience or musical ability needed! This class is intended for ages 15 and up only. A Sci-Fi September Event This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Build your own synthesizer step by step in this beginner electronics workshop led by Dogbotic.

events.title: Dogbotic Sound Petting Zoo
events.description: Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. How do you create the sound of a fictional planet, a malfunctioning starship, or a retro ray gun? For Sci-Fi September, the creative audio lab Dogbotic is setting up shop at Mountain View Public Library to show you the sounds of science fiction firsthand. Were hosting a sci-fi-themed sound petting zoo filled with a collection of unusual instruments and sound design props that you can try out yourself. Come dressed as your favorite sci-fi or fantasy character to really get in the mood! The program is free, and open to anyone ages 8 and up. A Sci-Fi September Event This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Try out sci-fi sound gadgets from creative audio lab Dogbotic during Sci-Fi September.

events.title: Short Story Social: "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora
events.description: Love the idea of a book club but don't have time for a whole novel? Join our Short Story Social, a relaxed "book club" for short-story fans and busy readers. We meet virtually on the fourth Thursday of each month to discuss one or two contemporary short stories (no more than 40 pages total). Participate from anywhere—jump in late or leave early if needed! Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link. 2026 Reading List June 25th- "The Shroud" in Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq July 23rd- "Mall of America" by Suzanne Wang in The Best American Short Stories 2024 August 27th- "A Sunny Place for Shady People" in A Sunny Place for Shady People by Mariana Enriquez September 24th- "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora in The Best American Short Stories 2025. * Also available in New England Review, Vol 45, No. 2-avaialble through Gale Academic Onefile with your library card. October 29th - "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" in Night Side of the River by Jeanette Winterson
events.blurb: Discuss Lauren Acampora's short story "Dominion" with fellow readers in a virtual short-story book club.

events.title: Amplify: Coco: Intro to Coding
events.description: Ever wanted to build your own video game or animation, With your friends, at the same time? Join us for a coding workshop to try Coco. Build, where you snap blocks together like puzzle pieces to create games, art, and more in real time! No experience needed, just bring your imagination. Let's build something awesome together! Grades 3-6. Library computers will be provided- you do not need to bring a laptop or other device to participate. This program is part of Amplify: Teen Voices, where teens who are passionate about a topic are mentored through the process of leading a library program.
events.blurb: Snap together digital blocks to build games and animations with friends in this Coco coding workshop.

events.title: Pages and Paws
events.description: Therapy reading dogs provide a comforting presence for children as they navigate the exciting realm of books. This initiative aims to build confidence, enhance literacy skills and instill a lifelong love for reading. Therapy dogs plan to visit on the first Friday of each month, but review our calendar to confirm dates. Limited registration is intentional to allow readers rewarding one-on-one reading time with a therapy dog. More details on your confirmed time-slot, and instruction to follow once registered. Ages 8-12.
events.blurb: Read aloud to visiting therapy dogs and build reading confidence in a relaxed library session.

events.title: Sew Sew Saturday
events.description: Need a sewing machine? The Library has sewing machines (model: Baby Lock Joy) and a serger (model: Brother 1034D) that are available for use within the Library on a drop-in basis. Whether you're working on a project or need to hem a garment, this casual, welcoming space is perfect for all skill levels. Volunteers are available to answer basic sewing questions. A limited number of supplies, such as scissors and thread, are provided. You are welcome to bring your own thread if you require a particular color. No registration required -- just bring your materials and drop in! This event is intended for adults, ages 18 and up. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Drop in to use the library's sewing machines and serger for your own hemming or sewing projects.

events.title: The Financial Side of Estate Planning: Beyond Wills and Trusts
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Most people think of estate planning as a legal task a will, a trust, a folder in a drawer. But many of the decisions that determine how your assets actually reach your family are financial ones, made on account forms and beneficiary designations years apart. What you'll learn: What legal documents do... And don't. Wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and healthcare directives: what each one accomplishes, and where its authority stops. How your assets actually transfer. Why beneficiary designations and account titling often decide who receives what - no matter what your will says. Overlooked areas that cause issues. Outdated beneficiaries, joint ownership problems, blended families, digital footprints, overlooked retirement rules and uncoordinated advice. Taxes, family, and legacy goals. How inherited retirement accounts are taxed, and how to coordinate family, charitable, and legal decisions into a cohesive plan. Every attendee receives complimentary resources, including an Estate Planning Readiness Checklist to organize their own information. Who should attend: Retirees Those approaching retirement Parents and grandparents Anyone who has accumulated assets and wants to protect their family We are also hosting the same workshop on Thursday, October 8 at 2:00 p.m. Presented by Daniel L. Foss, Ch FC, CLU.
events.blurb: Learn the financial decisions behind estate planning that go beyond wills and trusts.

events.title: Planning Your Cool Vegetable Garden in Our Mediterranean Climate
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Did you know that we can grow cool season vegetables in Santa Clara County? Its true! With our cool (but not cold) rainy season we can grow all sorts of vegetables like greens such as lettuce, chard and kale, to cruciferous vegetables like broccoli or cauliflower to root vegetables like beets, carrots and radishes. Come learn what you can grow with Matt Hall, UC Master Gardener. He will go over the basics such as soil, water and fertilizing requirements, and show all of the different plants that do great here. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn which cool-season vegetables like lettuce, chard, and kale thrive in Santa Clara County's climate.

events.title: Intro to 3D Printing: Science Fiction Edition
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Learn how 3D printing works and go through the full process of preparing and printing a small object associated with science fiction. Choose a 3D model, use slicing software to set it up, and help start the print on the librarys 3D printers. No prior 3D printing experience is needed but basic computer skills are expected. Ages 13 and up. A Sci-Fi September Event
events.blurb: Learn 3D printing basics by choosing, slicing, and printing a small sci-fi themed object.

events.title: Mid-Autumn Festival Chinese Calligraphy Workshop
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival with a hands-on Chinese calligraphy workshop! Whether you're a beginner or have experience, you will learn how to hold the brush, master basic strokes, and create calligraphic artwork while embracing the festive spirit. Ages 12 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Pick up a brush and learn Chinese calligraphy basics at this Mid-Autumn Festival workshop at the library.

events.title: Sewing with FabMo: Robot Aprons
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Join us in creating robot aprons using upcycled fabric. Alternative apron designs, such as flowers, will also be possible. This craft project will be led by Fab Mo volunteer, Bhanu Gomatam. This class is intended for adults, ages 18 and up. A Sci-Fi September event. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Sew a robot-themed apron from upcycled fabric with a FabMo volunteer guiding the project.

events.title: Cascada de Flores: El Abuelo (Ages 2-13)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Cascad-ita de Flores: Stories, Song & Dance presents... Original stories told in Spanish & English, using song, a variety of musical instruments, dance, theater and sweet characters of traditional Mexican & Latin American cultures. El Abuelo (aka The Tree and the Donkey who loved to sing) is an original story that celebrates Mexican traditional music and dance. It tells the story of a lonely tree and a donkey who loves to sing. Their music attracts the birds, the animals and one special human: el Abuelito (grandfather). Children and their families are invited to sing, dance and play with traditional songs and dances from various regions of Mexico. The audience will sing like owls, dance like vultures and laugh along with the humorous grandfather, Abuelo, while exploring themes from life and death in nature and instrument building. Join us in the Children's Room for this wonderful music show for the whole family!
events.blurb: Watch a bilingual Spanish and English performance of stories, song, dance, and theater from Latin American traditions.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Tiger's Wife, by Tea Obreht. In a Balkan country meding from the war, Natalia, a young doctor, is compelled to unravel the mysterious circumstances surrounding her berloved grandfathers recent death. Searching for clues, she turns to his worn copy of The Jungle Book and the stories he told her of his encounters over the years with the deathless man. But most extraordinary of all is the story her grandfather never told her - the legend of the tigers wife. The Monday Morning bookclub meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time. Sign up for our newsletter here.
events.blurb: Discuss Tea Obreht's The Tiger's Wife with fellow readers at the library's book club.

events.title: Cookbook Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: September's theme is in a bun! Each month we have a theme that you are free to interpret however you'd like. Choose a recipe to make from one of the many cookbooks or other resources in our collection- don't worry, we'll have plenty of suggestions for you! Then we'll meet to talk about books and cooking and enjoy each other's company. Photos of your finished dish are encouraged but not required. This month we're exploring all formats of buns! Whether you have them with a hot dog or burger, rolled up with cinnamon and brown sugar, sandwiching any number of fillings, or stuffed with meat or veggies and steamed, there are tons of ways to have your food in a bun. Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! Come to our meeting ready to talk all about what you made and the book you used. Don't forget to sign up for our Cookbook Club newsletter to get all the latest updates and cookbook suggestions! You can sign up for any of our newsletters here.
events.blurb: Cook a dish tied to this month's theme, then meet up to swap notes and taste each other's takes.

events.title: Informed Community Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! September's book will be All-American Nativism: How the Bipartisan War on Immigrants Explains Politics as We Know It, by Daniel Denvir From the publisher's website: It is often said that with the election of Donald Trump nativism was raised from the dead. After all, here was a president who organized his campaign around a rhetoric of unvarnished racism and xenophobia. Among his first acts on taking office was to block foreign nationals from seven predominantly Muslim countries from entering the United States. But although his actions may often seem unprecedented, they are not as unusual as many people believe. This story doesn't begin with Trump. For decades, Republicans and Democrats alike have employed xenophobic ideas and policies, declaring time and again that illegal immigration is a threat to the nations security, wellbeing, and future. The profound forces of all-American nativism have, in fact, been pushing politics so far to the right over the last forty years that, for many people, Trump began to look reasonable. As Daniel Denvir argues, issues as diverse as austerity economics, free trade, mass incarceration, the drug war, the contours of the post 9/11 security state, and, yes, Donald Trump and the Alt-Right movement are united by the ideology of nativism, which binds together assorted anxieties and concerns into a ruthless political project. All-American Nativism provides a powerful and impressively researched account of the long but often forgotten history that gave us Donald Trump. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.
events.blurb: Join a group discussion on current social, economic, and political issues over this month's chosen book.

events.title: Nature Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Nature lovers and science enthusiasts, we invite you to be part of our Nature Book Club! Every two months, well explore nonfiction books about nature and science, and compare notes in a friendly, welcoming discussion. August's book is The Wild Dark, by Craig Childs. About The Wild Dark: At a time when most people on Earth live in regions of acute light pollution, Craig Childs takes us on a journey to rediscover the awesome power of night itself. Seeking not the absence of light, but the presence of the universe, master storyteller Craig Childs sets out to bike from the blinding lights of the Las Vegas Strip to one of the darkest spots in North America. A fearless explorer of both the natural world and the human imagination, Childs guides us on a quest to rediscover the heavens and to ask: What does it do to us to not see the night sky? The Wild Dark is at once an adventure story, a field guide, and a celebration of the awesome power of night itself, inviting us to look up and to look inward, eyes wide and sparkling with stars. Craig Childs has published more than a dozen critically acclaimed books, including The Secret Knowledge of Water, Atlas of a Lost World, Virga & Bone, and Tracing Time. Many of his books have won awards including Reading the West Book Award, Southwest Book of the Year, Foreword Indies medalist, the Orion Book Award, and more. Childs lives in southwest Colorado.
events.blurb: Discuss nonfiction nature and science reads with fellow enthusiasts in a friendly, informal group setting.

events.description: October's theme is cake or pie! Each month we have a theme that you are free to interpret however you'd like. Choose a recipe to make from one of the many cookbooks or other resources in our collection- don't worry, we'll have plenty of suggestions for you! Then we'll meet to talk about books and cooking and enjoy each other's company. Photos of your finished dish are encouraged but not required. Are you Team Cake or Team Pie? Both? This month we'll be showing our team spirit by making either a cake or a pie, depending on which team you're on. You can make it sweet or savory, big enough for a crowd or small enough to be held in your hand- it's up to you! Think a Swedish smrgstrta or a savory hand pie, or one of the many, many cupcake recipes available. Or if you really are Team Both, you might consider attempting the legendary cherpumple! Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! Come to our meeting ready to talk all about what you made and the book you used. Don't forget to sign up for our Cookbook Club newsletter to get all the latest updates and cookbook suggestions! You can sign up for any of our newsletters here.
events.blurb: Bring a homemade cake or pie based on a cookbook recipe and taste everyone's takes on this month's theme.

events.title: Fratello Marionettes: Spooktacular (All Ages)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: At the Fratello Marionettes show, you will not only be amused and entertained, but will appreciate the very niche artistry of making the marionettes by hand, and the skill and craft of performing with them. Their Halloween variety show is family-friendly fun for all ages. The show features happy ghosts, Frankenstein, the Purple People Eater, a not-so-scary spider and more…. And of course, no Halloween show would be complete without a witch! Special care is taken to make this production a kid-friendly experience.
events.blurb: Watch hand-crafted marionettes perform a Halloween variety show built for audiences of all ages.

events.title: Girls Who Code
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: The Los Gatos Library has partnered with @Girls Who Code to create a club meant for people ages 12-18 to learn to code and change the world! What will I Learn? Our middle and high school Clubs encourage you to impact the community in a positive way through code. In order to build the skills you need to make an impact, you will learn how to code from our fun online tutorials and activities that will help you build animations, games, apps, and other things that you dream up! We have tutorials in Python, HTML/CSS, Java Script, and Java. Email: signup@gwc-losgatos.org to register.
events.blurb: Learn to code with other teens ages 12-18 and put your skills toward projects that impact the community.

events.title: Kids Mindful Art: Gratitude Trees (Ages 7-12)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Register for this fun and meditative art class with local arts instructor, Makiko Niwa! For this class we will be making Gratitude Trees, made in combination with dropper art. Before the students begin painting, Makiko will lead a brief gratitude meditation to inspire them to reflect on what they are thankful for, and introduce different colors to the meditation practice. Each drop will symbolize something they are grateful for. This class is open to children ages 7-12, and registration is required. This class will take place in the Technology Lab on the 2nd floor.
events.blurb: Make a dropper-art gratitude tree with instructor Makiko Niwa after a brief guided meditation.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Mountains Sing by Nguyen Phan Que Mai. Multi-generational take of the Tran family set against the backdrop of the Vietnam War. Vivid and steeped in the language and traditions of Vietnam, the book brings to life the human costs of the conflict from the point of view of the Vietnamese people themselves, while showing the true power of kindness and hope. A perfect follow up to The Women (our Nov. Selection), which brings to life the Vietnam War from an American perspective. The Monday Morning bookclub meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time. Sign up for our newsletter.
events.blurb: Discuss The Mountains Sing, a multi-generational novel of the Tran family during the Vietnam War.

events.title: Informed Community Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! November's book will be The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future and What We Can Do About It, by Robert Weissman From the publisher's website: Long-time corporate accountability crusaders Robert Weissman, Public Citizen president, and Joan Claybrook, Public Citizen president emeritus, investigate how giant corporations corrupt the policy-making process to block reforms favored by overwhelming majorities of the American people, and to enrich themselves through far-reaching corporate welfare schemes. The Corporate Sabotage of Americas Future And What We Can Do About It pulls back the curtain on the hidden tactics that big corporations employ to have their way in Washington, D. C. And state capitols and city halls across the nation. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.
events.blurb: Talk through pressing social, economic, and political issues with neighbors in this month's book discussion.

events.title: Sound Bath Healing Meditation
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Gaby Castro-Moroder is Back for another Sound Healing session! Come join us! Sound and music is used as a method of healing across various mediums. After being told for years that she has a healing presence, Gaby Castro started her sound healing journey and took certification courses in tuning forks, crystal sound bowls, and Tibetan sound bowls. Now she provides sound healing group and individual sessions under the name Song Pine and Stone, bringing her gentle presence to those in need. A group sound healing session runs about 60-90 minutes and includes the use of crystal sound healing bowls, Tibetan bowls, tuning forks, and various other sound healing instruments. Attendees will bring their own yoga mats, blankets, pillows, and whatever else they need to be comfortable during the session. Instruments will be played to create a sound bath and attendees will be encouraged to relax and enjoy the soft, soothing sounds. When the session ends, attendees will be asked to rehydrate and well discuss how the session felt for everyone. Age Range: Adults and Seniors Note: A consent form may be required and provided at the event. Attendees need to consult with their physician and get approval to attend healing sessions if they have metal in their bodies, suffered concussions, have a pacemaker, use an insulin pump, and the like. If in doubt, consult your physician before the session. The Los Gatos Library recognizes the diversity of our community and is committed to accessibility for all patrons. We strive to make every visitor feel comfortable by ensuring equal access to programs, services, and activities. If you require a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in a library program, please contact library@losgatosca.gov
events.blurb: Settle in with Gaby Castro-Moroder for a sound healing session using instruments and music to relax mind and body.

events.title: Social Stitching
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Come join fellow needlework and textile arts enthusiasts at the library! Crafters of all levels are welcome to bring their projects and chat, teach, learn, and make new friends at this casual weekly get together. This group is entirely self-directed and you are encouraged to bring your own tools and materials. If you are looking for some inspiration or don't know where to start, check out Creativebug - it's free with your library card and offers hundreds of project ideas and instructions.
events.blurb: Bring your needlework or textile project and stitch alongside other crafters of every skill level.

events.title: Crafty Corner (Ages 3-10)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Take some time out of your afternoon to imagine and create! Join us for a crafty activity in the Children's Room. (Previously known as Tinker Tuesday.) This program is geared towards children ages 3 through ~10. This program takes place on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 pm in the Children's Room. Please note that in August, November, and December, there is only 1 Crafty Corner event during those months. Check our calendar for accurate up-to-date information.
events.blurb: Make a hands-on craft in the Children's Room with kids ages 3 through 10.

events.title: Creative Break
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Have you been wanting to start journaling or using a planner but can't find the time or space to do it at home? Take some time for creativity at the Library and journal, work on your planner, or draw in your sketchbook. We'll provide some inspiration and fun stationery like washi tape, stickers, stamps, and pens, you bring your journal/planner/sketchbook/etc. This is a drop in program, so join us for 10 minutes if that's all you have, or stay for the whole time!
events.blurb: Bring your journal, planner, or sketchbook to the Library and create using provided stationery and inspiration.

events.title: Planning a Simple Native Garden for Beginners
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: California's native plants can be easy to grow, bloom year-round, and bring birds and butterflies to your yard; plus, they need 1/10 the water & maintenance of a traditional landscape. But where to start? Join us to learn each step of a plan for a successful, thriving native garden. Come away from this presentation with an easy checklist and all the resources you need to get started on your own yard.
events.blurb: Learn how to plan a native garden that saves water and draws birds and butterflies to your yard.

events.title: Storytime (Ages 0-5)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Early learners (babies and toddlers) and their families are welcome to join us at the Library for Storytime, where we will wiggle, sing, read, and dance together! Our program is developmentally appropriate for ages 0-5, and our goal is to create memories and special bonds between caregivers and their children, and to help with building skills for school readiness and for a future of loving books!
events.blurb: Wiggle, sing, read, and dance with your little one at this Library storytime for babies and toddlers.

events.title: Bug Power with Beetlelady! (Ages 6-12)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Register to join in on this artistic and heroic exploration of bugs with Dr. Stephanie Dole, also known as Beetlelady! events.title: Author Talk in Person - Interview with Past and Present Town Poets Laureate
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Come join us for a fun time as the Town's current Poet Laureate William Butler interviews our past Poet Laureate, Jen Siraganian, in celebration of her book Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead which won the 2026 Perugia Press Prize. events.blurb: Hear Poet Laureate William Butler interview past laureate Jen Siraganian and listen to her read from her prize-winning book.

events.title: Seated Sound Bath • Friday, September 25th • 7:00pm -Buy 1 & Bring a Friend!
events.description: September 25th - One ticket admits you + one guest at no additional charge. During this session, Julie will create a serene soundscape using singing bowls, gongs, and other therapeutic instruments, enveloping you in waves of sound that resonate through your entire being.

events.title: Indoor Family Storytime with Stay and Play
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. After Storytime concludes, families are invited to Stay & Play! For 30 minutes after storytime, special, age-appropriate toys will be available to keep the fun going. The librarian will also be there to answer any questions, recommend books, and talk to families! Free, with limited capacity. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.
events.blurb: Join stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities designed for the whole family at storytime.

events.title: Baby Lapsit Storytime
events.description: This program is for babies that are not yet walking confidently, and their caregivers. Come join us every Tuesday for Baby Lapsit Storytime! Baby Lapsit invites newborns, infants, babies, and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! The Storytime librarian will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. Lapsit Storytime 11:00 - 11:30 am Stay & Play 11:30 am - 12:00 pm Please note that this will be an indoor program. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free. Attendance limits follow SJPL guidelines.

events.title: Rose Garden Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library for ages 13-18, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. Rose Garden's Teens Reach group meets monthly on the second Tuesday with socializing and fun at 4:00 pm. Our in-person meet up plans for this school year include: Teen Volunteer Opportunities Election for Advisory Board Community Youth Engagement Games & Activities Snacks Guest Speakers Bring a friend, and learn more about what to expect with volunteering this year. If you are new to volunteering with the San Jose Public Library, please visit the Teens Reach: Community Service webpage or more information and be sure to create your online volunteer account (click "Sign Me Up" under Rose Garden Branch).

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Do you want to build your English language skills and your confidence? This beginning non-credit ESL course is Free! ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1 What will you learn in this class? This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information Starts: August 25, 2026 Ends: December 10, 2026 Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday Time: 10:30 AM. -12:30 PM Instructor: Michelle N. Henninger Before the classes start, you must complete a Guided Self-Placement (GSP). This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice speaking, reading, and writing English in this beginning, non-credit ESL class taught with Evergreen Valley College.

events.title: Homework Club
events.description: Need help with your homework? Kindergarten through 8th grade students can come to Edenvale Branch Library's Homework Club to get coached by trained library volunteers. Students can get free help with their homework in subjects such as reading, writing, math, and social studies! ​ Homework Club at Edenvale Branch Library is scheduled for Tuesdays each week from 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM, except for the following dates because of City holidays and school breaks: September 29th November 3rd November 24th Homework Club will end on November 17th for the Fall Semester and take a break for the Winter Holidays. The schedule for the Spring semester will be determined and posted in December 2026. Free. No registration is required; however, Homework Club has a limited capacity. Services will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis. As a result, students might not be coached one-on-one for the whole duration of the program depending on volunteer availability. If we do not have enough tutors, students will be redirected to Tutor.com, a library resource.

events.title: After-School STEaM
events.description: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons in at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEa M adventure every week. Active engagement with STEa M promotes academic success. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Aug 18 - The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing & Pepper Experiment Participants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap. Aug 25 - Logic Games Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. ***please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been Rescheduled for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly*** Sept 1 - Marble Run Fun Harness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run. Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (***please note topic change***) In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up. Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time) Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients. Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch. Sept 22 - Mental Math: Multiplication Children have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition. Oct 6 - Wind Turbine Engineering In this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Oct 13 - Paper Rockets Learn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest! Participants will learn about propulsion and list then create their own rockets. Oct 20 - Properties of Water (Science from Scientists) Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion and surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique properties of water. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program. Oct 27 - Mental Math: Doubling Down Learn some methods of doubling numbers and how that relates to multiplication skills. Nov 3 - Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper Planes In this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze Runner Teach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes. Nov 17 - Logic Games Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Nov 24 - Mental Math: Triples Dec 1 - Let's Build Parachutes In this workshop, participants will build parachutes of different shapes, sizes and material, and observe the impact of their design. They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Dec 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.

Our Tech Mentor can help you with: Basic smartphone, tablet, and computer help Setting up and using Email Downloading and using apps Making video calls (Zoom, Face Time, Google Meets, etc.) Browsing the internet (search engine basics, making simple searches, etc.) Navigating the SJPL website and digital resources *Please note: Tech Mentor support is limited to basic technology questions. Appointments are required. To make an appointment, call 408-808-3073 or email Caitlin Bosworth at c aitlin. Bosworth@sjlibrary.org.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help with smartphones, email, video calls, and browsing from a Tech Mentor at Educational Park Library.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. They are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K to3 and will be held in the Children's area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Read one-on-one or in a small group with a volunteer at Alviso Library's Reading to Children program.

events.title: Reading to Children: Special Baby Edition
events.description: Reading to Children: Special Baby Edition is a volunteer-led program for newborns, infants, babies, and their caregivers. Learn together and strengthen bonds through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. After the program, we we invite you to stay and play. The volunteer will join in the fun with special toys, giving babies and parents time to connect. Reading to Children: Special Baby Edition: 11 to 11:20 a.m. Stay & Play: 11:20 a.m. to noon No registration required. This program will cap at 25 participants to create a calm and comfortable environment for young children.
events.blurb: Bond with your baby through songs, rhymes, and books at Cambrian Library, then stay to play afterward.

events.title: Reading Buddy in English & Spanish
events.description: Help your child build confidence and strengthen their English or Spanish reading skills in a fun and supportive environment! Children in kindergarten through 3rd grade are invited to read aloud in English or Spanish to trained teen volunteers who will offer encouragement and help with pronunciation when needed. Whether your child is a fluent English or Spanish reader or is still building their confidence, Reading Buddy in English and Spanish provides a welcoming space to practice reading skills, celebrate bilingual literacy, and foster a lifelong love of reading—especially for students enrolled in dual-language immersion programs. Recommended for: Children in grades K–3 and their caregivers. Please note: Caregivers must remain in the Children's Area during the program.
events.blurb: Read aloud in English or Spanish to trained teen volunteers at Willow Glen Library's Reading Buddy program.

events.title: One-On-One Tech Help (English or Tiếng Việt)
events.description: Offered in English, or Tiếng Việt. Do you need help using a computer? Want to set up an email account? Stop by the Santa Teresa Branch Library for a session with our experienced volunteer! They can assist you with basic tech issues, such as: Setting up an email account, composing & sending emails, using email attachments Web searches and basic data entry Learning the basics of Microsoft Word and Excel and web-based productivity software such as Google docs Using the library's pay-for-print and photocopy machines Downloading apps on your phone or tablet And much more! You are welcome to bring your own device, such as a laptop, phone or tablet, or you can use one of our computers. Free, No Registration Required Ada Accommodation Requests
events.blurb: Get one-on-one tech help in English or Tiếng Việt from an experienced volunteer at Santa Teresa Library.

events.title: Family Movie Club - Finding Nemo
events.description: Please join us for Family Movie Club at the Joyce Ellington Branch as we watch Finding Nemo, an animated adventure about a father fish who travels across the ocean to find his son, Nemo, after he is captured by a diver. Families are invited to relax and enjoy this fun movie together in a welcoming community setting. Popcorn will be provided, and we will have coloring pages available for those who prefer a quiet activity during the movie. Free. No registration required. The program is sponsored by the Friends of the Joyce Ellington Library.
events.blurb: Watch Finding Nemo with your family at the Joyce Ellington Branch, an animated tale of a father searching the ocean for his son.

events.title: TeenHQ Poster Printing
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Wanna make that idea into a piece of wall art? Create a poster size print using Teen Hq Maker Space's HP Design Jet Studio, 36" Printer. Each participant can create one 24"x36" poster to take home per month. For images found online, ensure they are "large" enough for good print quality. Look for images that are at a minimum of 2,000 x 2,000 px. Create a collage of images or add effects on Canva. Be sure your canvas size is 24in x 36in. This program is free. No pre-registration required. This program is specifically for Middle and High Schoolers. Adult caregivers and younger siblings will be asked to sit in the Teen Reading Room while they wait.
events.blurb: Print your own 24x36 poster on the Teen HQ Maker Space's giant HP printer at King Library.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) 502: Listening & Speaking
events.description: ESL Listening & Speaking 1 (Non-credit, high-beginning level ESL course). Students will learn to pronounce basic words accurately, communicate effectively, understand and use basic grammar structures, and build their foundational vocabulary. To Enroll, You Must: Complete and pass the Self-Guided Computer Assessment ( This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. To ensure accurate results, the GSP should be completed independently and in a quiet setting, without assistance from others). Submit the registration form To schedule your assessment appointment, send an email to marcela. Guevara@sjlibrary.org ESL 502 Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026 Ends: December 10, 2026 Class Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday Time: 5:15 PM – 6:45 PM Instructor: TBD No classes on: Veteran's Day - Wednesday, Nov 11th, 2026 Thanksgiving - Thursday, Nov 26th, 2026 We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary in this high-beginning ESL listening and speaking class with Evergreen Valley College.

events.title: Indoor Music and Movement
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: This program is best for children ages 2-8 with their caregivers, but all children with caregivers are welcome. Join us every Wednesday for Music and Movement at the King Library Children's Room! Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages; we invite the entire family to participate in early literacy activities and develop motor skills through song and movement activities - sometimes with scarves, shakey eggs, and rhythm sticks! Music and Movement is a high energy Storytime - a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning and movement. We'll start with a story, then move and groove to our monthly playlist. Free, with limited capacity. Program finishes by 6:10pm. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Sing, dance, and play instruments with your little one at King Library's Music and Movement session in the Children's Room.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as: Printing Using email Connecting to Wi-Fi Creating documents Accessing library resources Registering for an appointment is optional. If you register for an appointment, it can start at any time between 3 p.m. to 4:30 pm. Please contact Sarah Kishler at sarah. Kishler@sjlibrary.org or 408-808-3075 to let us know what time you would like to come in. When there is space, walk-ins starting between 3 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. are also welcome.
events.blurb: Sit down with a tech mentor at East SJ Carnegie Library for one-on-one help with printing, email, or Wi-Fi.

events.title: Playdates for Children and Their Caregivers
events.description: Join us every Wednesday for weekly playdates. Kids get to practice early social skills like sharing, taking turns, imitation of play, and joint attention while caregivers get a chance to connect. Don't miss out on this chance to celebrate the joys of play while connecting with other families in the community. It's a wonderful way to learn through play and create lasting memories together! 1st Wednesday: Cars 2nd Wednesday: Superhero Obstacle Course (ages 3-8) 3rd Wednesday: LEGO Duplo Blocks 4th Wednesday: Cars 5th Wednesday: LEGO Duplo Blocks Recommended for children ages 2 – 6 years old.
events.blurb: Bring your child to Seven Trees Library and practice sharing, turn-taking, and play with other families.

events.title: One-on-One Computer Help with our Tech Mentor
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Stop by the West Valley Branch Library for one-on-one computer help with our experienced, friendly Tech Mentor! Our Tech Mentor volunteer can help you with basic computer issues like: Learning the basics of Microsoft Word and Excel; Setting up an email account; Using social networking services like Facebook; Submitting an online job application: Downloading an e-book from the library's web site; And much more! No appointment necessary. Patrons will be helped on a first-come, first-served basis. Appointment times may be limited depending on patron demand.
events.attendanceNote: No appointment necessary. Patrons will be helped on a first-come, first-served basis. Appointment times may be limited depending on patron demand.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one computer help at West Valley Library, from email setup to basic Word and Excel skills.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Storytime is a fun and interactive experience designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. This program promotes the joys of reading and learning for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Stay after storytime for our Stay and Play session, where kids can enjoy hands-on activities, toys, and social playtime together. Free, with limited capacity. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club: Intermediate
events.description: ¡Ven a practicar hablar y escuchar inglés en persona en la Biblioteca Latinoamericana! Desarrolla habilidades de conversación con otros estudiantes de nivel intermedio en un lugar acogedor y respetuoso. Este programa es para adultos solamente. Cada sesión está dirigida por personal de la biblioteca que habla español y ingles. Gratis. No es necesario registrarse. Solicitud de Accesibilidad Ada Come practice speaking and listening in English in-person at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana! Build conversation skills with other intermediate level adult learners in a welcoming and respectful environment. Each session is led by library staff who speaks Spanish and English. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice spoken English with fellow intermediate learners at Biblioteca Latinoamericana's conversation club.

events.title: STEAM Club
events.description: Join us every Wednesday afternoon for a new STEAM adventure, from robots to engineering to science to making. Sept 2 - Sphero Messages Sept 9 - Paper Towers Sept 16 - Augmented Reality Sept 23 - Power of 2 Appropriate for ages 8 to 12. To manage space, adults are asked to stay outside of the class. If your child isn't able to participate independently, Junior STEAM (Thursdays) or Family STEAM (Saturdays) may be a better fit. Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.

events.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime

events.description: Infant and Toddler Storytime invites children and their caregivers to wiggle, rhyme, and sing with diverse books, songs, and fingerplays that encourage language, play, and exploration. This program is geared for children 0 to 3 years of age and their parents/caregivers, but all children are welcome! After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! Until 12pm the Storytime librarian and special toys will be on the Children's Room floor to keep the fun going. Meet new friends, play with toys, chat, get book recommendations, and maybe even create something! Storytime 11:00-11:30am Stay & Play 11:30am-12:00pm This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Wiggle, rhyme, and sing with your infant or toddler at King Library's storytime for ages 0 to 3.

events.title: Special Storytime with Birdie the Brave
events.description: Join local author Lena Strickling and her therapy dog, Birdie, for a storytime about dogs, heroes, and the importance of asking for help. Birdie the Brave follows a therapy dog extraordinaire who uses her superpower of listening and loving to comfort firefighters, police officers, nurses, teachers, and more in the town of Hero Heights. This heartwarming story teaches children about empathy, emotional support, and the importance of talking about feelings — reminding them that it's okay to need help, even when you're a hero. Seating for Special Storytimes is available on a first-come, first-served basis. Access to the children's picture book collection will be limited during the program. Please ask staff for help if needed. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.

events.blurb: Meet author Lena Strickling and her therapy dog Birdie at Pearl Avenue Library for a storytime about courage and asking for help.

events.title: Natural Solutions for Calming Inflammation & Feeling Unstoppable
events.description: 3 Hidden Causes of Inflammation & 3 Powerful Tools You'll Need to Take Back Your Health! Inflammation is behind all sorts of symptoms: Body pain, excess weight, allergies, digestive issues (gas, bloating, irregular BM's), low or inconsistent energy, headaches and more. Licensed nutritionist Rebecca Hazelton will share: What the 3 hidden causes of inflammation are so you can stop feeding the inflammatory cycle. How a clean, anti-inflammatory diet is not one-size fits all and how you can create the right anti-inflammatory diet for you! Lifestyle tools that will help you transform your inflammation, weight, energy & other symptoms! Plus a free gift to help you take your health to the next level! All are welcome. No registration needed. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org
events.blurb: Hear a licensed practitioner explain hidden causes of inflammation and natural tools to manage it at Cupertino Library.

The class focuses on improving English speaking and listening skills. The ESL class is taught at a beginner to intermediate level. Regular attendance is required. events.description: Bring your dancing feet to the Mitchell Park Library on Wednesday evenings for Music & Movement with Librarian Celina. Build early literacy skills through movement, songs, and dance. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. events.title: Qigong
events.description: Presenter: Amy Yang Certified Qigong Instructor International Neijin Qigong Academy Instruction will be in English and Mandarin Thursdays, August 6 through October 8, 2026 11am--12:30pm. Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov ( Diary of an Invasion ) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Bachman - January The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October What We Can Know by Ian Mc Ewan - November The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December Sign up for the library newsletter and never miss another program! events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. Http://danielebd.com/

events.title: AI Scams & Misinformation: How to Spot What's Real
events.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the way we communicate, but it is also making scams and misinformation more convincing than ever. In this free interactive workshop, participants will learn how to identify AI-generated images, videos, and voice recordings. They will also understand the real-world impacts that AI-generated misinformation can have, and learn ways to mitigate its impacts In addition to AI-generated misinformation, this workshop will also cover broader digital literacy skills, including fact-checking, online scams, and more. Participants will learn how to identify reliable sources, search for the origin of a claim, judge the quality of an article or post, and be equipped to navigate the online world. The presentation is designed to be easy to understand, engaging, and appropriate for community members with little or no technical background.

events.title: Adult Non-Fiction Book Discussion: A History of the World in Six Glasses
events.description: Open to all adults who enjoy reading and discussing Non-fictional Literature. In September the Adult Non fiction Book Discussion Group will talk about A History of the World in Six Glasses by Tom Standage (2005) Standage writes that each epoch of our world saw the origin of a form of a popular drink we now take for granted. When humans first became settled into farming communities rather than hunting and gathering, surplus grain stores lead to the development of beer. The Greeks and Romans discovered how to make wine from grapes—a discovery that went through several centuries of development. The Arabic world studied distillation and contributed spirits—a form of drink that could withstand long sea voyages. The Arabs also contributed coffee, which rapidly spread north and west to Europe in the 16th and 17th centuries. Tea was the contribution of the British Empire during the resulting from their extensive colonialization of India and China. Lastly, Coca-Cola which started as a medicinal drink in the American South, became a symbol of American 20th Century Capitalism. The Adult Non-fiction Book Discussion meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. events.title: Travel Program: South Pacific Islands Expedition
events.description: Join Bruce Berger and Pam Perkins as they share video and photos from their 24-day expedition to remote islands in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. We will visit isolated villages on beautiful unspoiled islands, meet warm and welcoming locals, and witness tribal ceremonies. One highlight includes the spectacular river encounter with dozens of warrior canoes, approaching the Asmat village where Michael Rockefeller disappeared in 1961. Important WWII history is remembered at Rabaul and Guadalcanal. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. events.title: UC Master Gardeners: Gardening with Mediterranean Ornamentals
events.description: You may be familiar with California Native ornamental plants, but did you know that there are Mediterranean climates around the world that have the same growing conditions as we have here in Santa Clara County? They produce many beautiful ornamentals that grow very well here and do not need much water and little or no fertilizer. October and November are the very best months for putting these plants in the ground. Come and join UC Master Gardener Martha Carpenter to learn about beautiful, hardy, ornamental plants from other Mediterranean climates, as well as some California natives, that would be great additions to your waterwise garden! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Some Strange Music Draws Me In
events.description: In September, the Cupertino Library Book Discussion Group will talk about the coming of age novel Some Strange Music Draws Me In: A Novel by Griffin Hansberry (2024). After their mother's death in 2019, Max and his Fox-News addicted sister work to clear out their family's home in working class Swaffham, Massachusetts. Max is currently suspended from his teaching job at a privileged private school in Massachusetts after having been accused of using transphobic language against students. Ironic, considering that Max grew up as Melanie. Stuck in a town that is less than accepting of its LGBTQIA+ community, Max reminisces about 1984, and his earlier friendship with Sylvia, a bold transgender woman who helped the girl he was then find the courage to make her transition. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month on the third Wednesday morning at 11 am, and the third Thursday Evening at 7pm. All meetings are held in room 201B. Adults of all ages are welcome. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Qigong
events.description: Presenter: Amy Yang Certified Qigong Instructor International Neijin Qigong Academy Instruction will be in English and Mandarin Thursdays, August 6 through October 8, 2026 11am--12:30pm. Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Some Strange Music Draws Me In
events.description: In September, the Cupertino Library Book Discussion Group will talk about the coming of age novel Some Strange Music Draws Me In: A Novel by Griffin Hansberry (2024). After their mother's death in 2019, Max and his Fox-News addicted sister work to clear out their family's home in working class Swaffham, Massachusetts. Max is currently suspended from his teaching job at a privileged private school in Massachusetts after having been accused of using transphobic language against students. Ironic, considering that Max grew up as Melanie. Stuck in a town that is less than accepting of its LGBTQIA+ community, Max reminisces about 1984, and his earlier friendship with Sylvia, a bold transgender woman who helped the girl he was then find the courage to make her transition. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month on the third Wednesday morning at 11 am, and the third Thursday Evening at 7pm. All meetings are held in room 201B. Adults of all ages are welcome. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Dreaming with Your Eyes Open: Double Bill
events.description: Come join us in the beautiful Milpitas Library for an afternoon of surreal movies exploring social satire and self imprisonment. At 2:00 PM, we will be showing The Exterminating Angel ( El ángel exterminador), which centers around a dinner party whose guests can't seem to leave. As the night goes on the guests abandon social etiquette and fall into chaos. Created by surrealism's most influential director, Luis Buñuel, this satire is considered one of the best 1,000 movies ever made. (This movie is in Spanish with English subtitles) At 3:45 PM, we will be showing Synecdoche, New York, where Caden Cotard, an ailing theater director, tries to build a replica of the city and his life in a Manhattan warehouse in an attempt to direct it all. This program is part of the Surreal Film Series! Other events in the series: August 29: Alice in Wonderland and Fantastic Planet. October 17: The Blood of A Poet and Eraserhead.
events.blurb: Watch a double bill of surreal films, starting with The Exterminating Angel's trapped dinner party.

events.title: Poetry Open Mic
events.description: A Multilingual, Multigenerational Evening of Words & Voices Hosted by Thomas Célérier - Cupertino Poet Laureate Join us for an open and welcoming poetry afternoon at the Cupertino Library, where voices of all ages, cultures, and languages come together to share the power of the spoken and written word. This open mic celebrates poetry in all its forms, spoken, read, sung, remembered, or improvised. Whether you write in English, Spanish, Mandarin, Hindi, Tagalog, or another language close to your heart, you are warmly invited to share. Translations and explanations are welcome but never required. All generations are encouraged to participate and attend. Come listen, come read, come perform, or simply come to be present. This is a community space rooted in respect, curiosity, and the joy of language. All are welcome. No prior experience necessary. Plan for 1 or 2 poems to share in the language of your choice (with translation or not). This could be your own poem(s) or the one(s) from an author you like. Open to poets, storytellers, elders, youth, and first-time readers alike. Let's gather to listen deeply, celebrate difference, and honor the many languages that shape our community. We look forward to seeing you there! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, please cancel your registration as soon as you know you will not be able to attend, so people on the waitlist can register. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For September 20th: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Learn Science – Do Not Fear Death or Gods "It is impossible to get rid of our anxieties about essentials if we do not understand the nature of the universe and are apprehensive without some of the theological accounts. Hence it is impossible to enjoy our pleasures unadulterated without natural science." Principal Doctrine 12. "Dreams have neither divine character nor prophetic power but are generated by the influx of atomic images." Vatican Sayings 24. "Death means nothing to us, because that which has been broken down into atoms has no sensation and that which has no sensation is no concern of ours." Principal Doctrine 2. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Oxford University Press, 2023. Chs. 19 (pp. 202-210) and 20 (pp. 211-221); Epicurus. The Art of Happiness. Letter to Menoeceus, 123-127. Some Questions to Discuss: Why did Epicurus insist on the importance of learning science? What is Epicurus's definition of the irreligious person? What is death to us, according to Epicurus? Why would the topic of death occupy such a prominent place in the Epicurean philosophy of pleasure? Can our society be convinced by Epicurus's argument?
events.blurb: Discuss big questions about hustle, success and how we choose to live in this reading group.

The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) chapter of the American Needlepoint Guild was chartered on March 1, 1986. We meet monthly at the Milpitas Police Department Community Room. At our meetings we present programs which encourage and inspire members to explore new techniques in needlepoint, learn about design, color, texture and perspective, and provide an opportunity to network with others who share a passion for needlepoint.
