If you would like to find out more about SBN, please join us at one of our meetings or contact us at: sbnangcontact@gmail.com.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents Lessons in Fear
events.description: Does the solution to the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians rest in the classroom rather than in the angry, fearful streets of the region? Can better answers be found in schools rather than political conferences? Lessons in Fear explores Israeli and Palestinian education from the ground up. In a media world obsessed with conflict, Lessons in Fear takes a humanized, behind-the-scenes look at how ordinary kids are educated in one of the world's trouble spots. The film looks carefully at the lives of students and teachers, who find themselves on the front lines intellectually and physically. Their battleground is one of knowledge and self-examination. Their challenges are a deeply engrained culture of violence, the denial of history and legacies of hatred, propaganda and segregation. Lessons in Fear is not a litany of wrongs. The film is a character driven portrait of courage in action as it presents an unvarnished look at the struggle to make education a positive force in Israel and the Palestinian Territories. James Cullingham is an educator, award-winning documentary filmmaker, a widely published writer, and seasoned national broadcaster. Cullingham is coordinator and a professor in the Journalism Broadcast program at the School of Communication Arts of Seneca College in Toronto. His documentaries concerning social justice, politics, history, and popular culture have been screened around the world. Cullingham has been published by Canada's leading newspapers and magazines. He appears as a guest on a number of Canadian public affairs and cultural television programs. In 2003-2005, Cullingham earned a Masters degree in history at the University of Toronto. He is currently pursuing doctoral studies in history at Toronto's York University Ontario with an Honor's Degree in Native Studies and French. He is an accomplished wilderness canoeist and avid hiker. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch Lessons in Fear, a documentary examining Israeli and Palestinian education amid ongoing conflict.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, please cancel your registration as soon as you know you will not be able to attend, so people on the waitlist can register. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For October 4th: Topic: Desires - Natural, Necessary, and Unnecessary. Greed for Life and Wealth "Some desires are natural and necessary, others natural but not necessary, still others neither natural nor necessary but generated by senseless whims." Principal Doctrine 29. "A person is made unhappy either by fear or by endless and vain desire. The man who curbs these can attain for himself the blessed gift of reason." Fragment 74. "All desires that do not lead to physical pain if not satisfied are unnecessary, and involve cravings that are easily resolved when they appear to entail harm or when the object of desire is hard to get." Principal Doctrine 30. "Nothing is sufficient for the man to whom the sufficient is too little." Vatican Sayings 68 "Everyone departs this life as though he had only just been born." Vatican Sayings 60. "There is also a limit to frugality. The man unable to consider this suffers a similar end as the man who indulges in excess." Vatican Sayings 63. "Not the youth, but the old man who has lived life well, is to be deemed happy. The youth in his prime is made distraught and baffled by fortune; the old man, as though in port in his old age, has brought safely into harbor the goods he scarcely hoped for before, and has secured them with unfailing gratitude." Vatican Sayings 17. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 5 (pp. 42-53), 10 (pp. 103-115), and 14 (pp. 145-155). Some Questions to Discuss: What is the criterion that Epicurus suggested for discriminating between desires? "What will happen to me if the object of my desire is achieved? What will happen if it is not?" from Epicurus, Vatican Sayings 71. Does Epicurus advise his reader to be ascetic? Can our society accept Epicurus's argument against excessive wealth? Can we offer the alternative argument in support of excessive wealth? In our society, what can drive the desire to live if not forever, then for 300 or even 500 years? (These numbers have been recently stated in interviews with some enthusiasts of longevity research. See, for example, this article ).
events.blurb: Read and discuss big questions about hustle, success, and how we choose to live with fellow attendees.

events.title: San Francisco Opera Guild: Manon preview
events.description: Join us for a preview and presentation by Rebecca Plack of the San Francisco Opera's upcoming performance of Manon by Jules Massenet. Manon is young, beautiful, and has a taste for the finer things … which is why her family is sending her to a convent. En route to her new life, she falls for the handsome Chevalier des Grieux and they run away to Paris, the city of love. But their youthful ardor is threatened by fatherly disapproval, and Manon finds herself with a choice to make: wait alone in poverty or embrace the wealth of a new lover? Manon composer Jules Massenet 's soaring score captures the intensity of young love as Manon and Des Grieux's relationship endures twist after turn. Manon must navigate a path that careens between the radiant glow of love and the allure of wealth. Soprano and musicologist Rebecca Plack is Professor of Opera Studies and Music History at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music; she has also taught at the Vancouver International Song Institute. She has performed solo recitals for the International Great Romantics Festival in Hamilton, Canada, at the ATER Forum Festival in Ferrara, Italy, and at the Franz Liszt Museum in Budapest; she has also given talks and lecture recitals at Oxford University and at meetings of the American Musicological Society. Her opera credits include leading and featured roles with Ithaca Opera and Sacramento Opera, as well as with the Caramoor and Aspen music festivals. She graduated magna cum laude from Princeton University, received her MM from the Manhattan School of Music, and earned her doctorate at Cornell University, where her dissertation explored connections between vocal technique and musical style in recordings of German Lieder. She lives in Davis, CA, where she maintains a private voice studio. Registration means you will receive a reminder email the day before but registration is not required.
events.blurb: Hear Rebecca Plack preview San Francisco Opera's Manon, the story of a young woman bound for a convent.

events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov ( Diary of an Invasion ) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. Http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Discuss the group's chosen graphic novel with fellow readers age 16 and up at Mitchell Park Library.

events.title: Writers Helping Writers: From Memoir to Career Planning Book: A Journey of Discovery
events.description: How did a collection of short-story memoirs from the corporate world turn into a full-fledged career-planning book? Join author Korie Pelka for an open, interactive presentation on her wild, nonlinear path to publication. She'll pull back the curtain on how she discovered her voice, pinpointed her target reader, and clarified the impact she wanted her book to make. Expect real talk on all the foibles and missteps along the way—and how you can avoid them in your own journey. Korie Pelka holds a B. F. A. And M. A. In theater directing, which served her well during her 25-year career as a communications professional in Silicon Valley. In 2015 she left the corporate world to discover her own voice in her "third act." Today she is a certified career coach who has helped hundreds of clients navigate meaningful career transitions. Her book, Get Unstuck. Get Clear. Get Going. A Guide to Discovering the Next Stage in Your Career Journey, is a business career-planning book that provides an actionable framework for confidently navigating what's next in your life and career. Korie chronicles her third-act journey and her avid quest for the perfect gelato on her website www.koriepelka.com. California Writers Club-San Francisco Peninsula Branch members share their expertise on writing, editing, marketing, publishing and more. Writers Helping Writers resumes for their fourth year on the third Thursday of these months: October 15 January 21 March 18 May 20 Registration is not required, but if you register, you'll receive an email reminder the day before the event. Sign up for the library newsletter and never miss another program!
events.blurb: Hear author Korie Pelka discuss turning her corporate memoir stories into a full career-planning book at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, please cancel your registration as soon as you know you will not be able to attend, so people on the waitlist can register. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For October 18th: Topic: Desires - Natural, Necessary, and Unnecessary. Success, Ambition, Sex "One who understands the limits of the good life knows that what eliminates the pains brought on by need and what makes the whole of life perfect is easily obtained, so that there is no need for enterprises that entail the struggle for success." Principal Doctrine 21. "Great abundance is heaped up as the result of brutalizing labor, but a miserable life is the result." Fragment 73. "If there is intense striving after those physical desires that do not lead to pain if unfulfilled, this is because they arise from idle opinion; they fail to be dispelled, not because of their own nature but because of the vain fancies of humankind." Principal Doctrine 30. "Happiness and blessedness do not belong to abundance of riches or exalted position or offices or power, but to freedom from pain and gentleness of feeling and a state of mind that sets limits that are in accordance with nature." Fragment 85. "I learn from your letter that carnal disturbances make you excessively inclined to sexual intercourse. Well, so long as you do not break any laws or disturb well-established conventions or annoy any of your neighbors or wear down your body or use up your funds, you may carry out your own plans as you like. However, it is impossible not to be affected by at least one of these things. Sex never benefited any man, and it's a marvel if it hasn't injured him!" Vatican Sayings 51. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 13 (pp. 137-144) and 16 (pp. 171-179). Some Questions to Discuss: What effect do competitive relations and ambitions have on us as individuals and as a society? What does it mean to be successful for Epicurus? What would be counted as success in our society? How do we reason our understanding of success? Would we agree with Epicurus's argument on sexual desire?
events.blurb: Read and discuss big questions about hustle, success, and values with the Philosophy for Life group at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Neurosphere: Neuroscience and More! Grades 3-8
events.description: Come join teen-led group Neuro Sphere! Neuro Sphere is a community for curious 2nd-7th graders about medicine! There will be snacks- feel free to bring a friend! We're a group of high school students driven by a passion for neuroscience and the wonders of the brain. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through Neuro Sphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com This program is open for 2nd-7th graders only.

It is open to all levels of experience and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, please cancel your registration as soon as you know you will not be able to attend, so people on the waitlist can register. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7] Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?
events.blurb: Join a friendly reading and discussion group exploring big ideas about success, values, and how we choose to live.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.

Note: Registrations will be released for standby attendees at the start of the program. Please arrive on time. Project Humane Kind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, Transmilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at Sxsw and received critical acclaim. Trans Military was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, Side XSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to Side XSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch a documentary tracing Stasi surveillance in East Germany through Peter Keup's personal investigation into family secrets.

events.title: Mid-Autumn Festival Craft for Ages 5 - 12
events.description: Join us to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival with a paper lantern craft and treats. This program is designed for children ages 5 – 12. Registration is required. All materials will be provided. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Las Madres Playgroup
events.description: "Nothing substitutes for the ability to build friendships with parents who are faced with similar parenting issues." Join Las Madres Downtown/Rose Garden for a weekly Tuesday playgroup. Children can play in a safe environment in the Rose Garden Library Community Room and parents can connect and find/lend support to other parents in the Rose Garden and Downtown San Jose area. Learn more about Las Madres. This is a free event. No registration is required.
events.blurb: Bring your kids to play together while parents connect and share parenting experiences at this weekly playgroup.

events.title: Teen Craft & Connect
events.description: Looking to make new friends and have fun at the same time? Teen Craft & Connect (ages 12–18) is a welcoming weekly program created to help teens hang out, get creative, and build real connections in a friendly, relaxed setting. September 9 - Bedazzling mirrors September 16 - Decorating pencil pouches September 23 - Keychains September 30 - Glass suncatchers Free supplies provided while they last. No registration—just show up and be ready to have fun!
events.blurb: Hang out with other teens, get creative, and build connections at this weekly craft session for ages 12-18.

events.title: Beginning Sewing
events.description: Attendees will learn the basics of sewing machine usage and then make a small pillow. This program is for beginners who have not sewn before. The first 45 minutes will be focused on vocabulary and basics such as threading the machine. If you have some experience sewing, please come to our intermediate classes. Open to the first four to register. Fabric for pillows will be provided, however you may bring your own "fat quarter" 18" x 21" if you prefer.
events.blurb: Learn to thread and operate a sewing machine, then sew your own small pillow as a beginner.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Bring your dancing feet to the Mitchell Park Library on Wednesday evenings for Music & Movement with Librarian Celina. Build early literacy skills through movement, songs, and dance. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. This program is meant for families with children and no previous experience is needed! This week, we'll be celebrating Diwali with music in Hindi!
events.blurb: Sing, dance, and play instruments with Librarian Celina at this early-literacy music session for families.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Join us for a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners to practice and gain confidence speaking English. A volunteer facilitator guides the conversations. Topics range widely according to the interests of those who attend. All skill levels are welcome; however, this program is best suited for those with a basic ability to converse in English. The conversation club meets every Wednesday from 1 to 2 p.m. Free. Registration not required.
events.blurb: Practice speaking English on wide-ranging topics with a volunteer facilitator in a welcoming adult conversation group.

events.title: Baby Sign Language Storytime
events.description: It's storytime with a fun spin. Children will have a blast at this special storytime integrating language and movement with American Sign Language (ASL). No registration required. This program generously sponsored by the Friends of the Rose Garden Branch Library.

events.title: Friends of the Campbell Library Used Book Sale
events.description: Join us for the Friends of the Campbell Library used book sale! Items for sale include puzzles, games, hardback fiction books, children's books, romances, thrillers, audio books, DVDs, CDs, and a variety of 'how to' books. Pay cash, check, Zelle, card, or Venmo Remember to bring a bag for your purchases! Sign up to hear about more upcoming Book Sales at the Friends of the Campbell Library's website: Sales - Friends of the Campbell Library
events.blurb: Browse puzzles, games, books, DVDs, and CDs for sale to benefit the Friends of the Campbell Library.

events.title: Family Craft: Leaf Rubbing Watercolor Resist Art
events.description: Choose from a variety of leaves, create your own rubbings using crayon, and then use watercolor paint! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a the watercolor resist leaf rubbing art using leaves, crayons, paper, watercolor paints, and brushes. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Make watercolor resist leaf rubbing art with crayons and paint, a hands-on craft for kids ages 4 to 11.

events.title: Sunday CrafterNoon
events.description: All-ages arts and crafts! Adults, teens, and kids -- join us for an afternoon of relaxed crafting on the third Sunday of the month. Supplies are provided for you to explore a surprise art activity. This craft is self-directed; children must come with their responsible adult crafting-buddy. The room closes at 3:30 PM, so please give yourself enough time to finish your craft. Although if you like, you are welcome to complete it at home.
events.blurb: Drop in with your kids and craft a surprise art project together during this relaxed all-ages afternoon session.

events.title: Willow Glen Library Knitters
events.description: Do you enjoy working with yarn, knitting or crochet? Want to see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all things yarn, knitting and crochet? All hand needle crafts welcome. No training or supplies are provided, but if you need advice there are many experienced knitters who are happy to lend a hand. Grab your project and join us weekly in the Willow Glen Library Community Room. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting or crochet project and swap tips with other yarn crafters at the library.

events.title: Toddler Storytime
events.description: Stories and Songs for 1-2 year olds. This story time features lots of movement, singing, and action and is geared for very young toddlers who can no longer sit in laps! events.blurb: Sing, move, and hear stories with your toddler at this storytime made for 1 to 2 year olds.

events.title: Bay Area Quiz Club
events.description: Join the Bay Area Quiz Club for fun trivia and friendly competition! Bay Area Quiz Club (Baqc) is a volunteer run organization. Our quizzes take place from 2-6pm on the second Sunday of every month, at Mitchell Park Library, Palo Alto. It is free and open to everyone.

events.description: Make your own mini masterpieces at the library! Get to know other teens in your community and let your creative juices flow as you paint your own mini canvas. This program is for teens ages 13-18. While supplies last. One canvas per teen. All materials will be provided, but you're welcome to bring your own supplies. Free. No registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Santa Teresa Branch.
events.blurb: Paint your own mini canvas and meet other teens at this library craft session for ages 13 to 18.

events.title: Wee Love Art: Fall Leaf Sensory Painting in Baggies
events.description: Explore the colors and textures of autumn leaves in our sensory painting program! Using leaf-shaped cardstock and fall-inspired colors, children will create unique artworks while enhancing fine motor skills and fostering creativity. Guided by our librarians, kids will experiment with paint mixing and texture blending, promoting cognitive and social development. Join us for a fun-filled morning celebrating fall creativity!
events.blurb: Paint fall leaf shapes and explore autumn colors and textures in this sensory art program for kids.

events.title: Lotería at the Library!
events.description: It's Latine & Hispanic Heritage Month (September 15-October 15) and we're playing lotería at the Library! Lotería is a widely popular Mexican game, similar to bingo, where you match images called out on your board, marking it with a pinto bean and forming a pattern (row, column, diagonal, etc.). Whoever calls out "lotería" first wins the round and receives a prize and bragging rights. This event is for ages 8 and up.
events.blurb: Play lotería, matching images on your board with a pinto bean, for Latine and Hispanic Heritage Month.

events.title: Edenvale Branch Library Family Open House
events.description: Celebrate the back-to-school season at our Family Open House. Visit the Library and learn about programs and services for all ages. We'll have: Educational Resource Craft Activities Drawing to win a free back-to-school prizes - must be present to receive prize. Recommended for students and families. Free - No Registration required. Sponsored by the Friends of the Edenvale Branch Library Ada Accommodation Requests
events.blurb: Tour the library, learn about programs and services for all ages, and try a craft activity for a chance to win a prize.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interactions with our reading Volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading aloud with our volunteer. Please note, this is not a tutoring session. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Meet a reading volunteer for one-on-one or small group storytime and practice reading aloud yourself.

events.title: Saturday Board Games Day
events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. Attendees can bring their own games to play or jump-in with others. Please bring your own snacks and drinks to fuel an afternoon of marathon gaming in the El Camino Room. Presented by The Bay Area Boardgames Meetup Group. Masks are not required in the Palo Alto Libraries, but are recommended.

events.description: Create your own tree painting using the pointillism technique! Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, tatting, or bobbin lace project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the community room.

events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteers Mike, Sally & Matt. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Hear kids read one-on-one or in small groups with volunteers Mike, Sally, and Matt at Willow Glen Library.

events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. events.blurb: Watch kids read one-on-one or in small groups with a librarian at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Jewelry Making-STEM
events.description: Be a Mini Maker! Join us for a creative jewelry making craft workshop. Learn how to design and create your own unique bracelet using colorful beads and charms, and take home your very own beaded bracelet. Materials will be provided. Recommended for ages 7 and up. Perfect for beginners and experienced crafters! ADA Accommodation Request
events.blurb: Design and string your own beaded bracelet with charms at this hands-on jewelry making workshop for young makers.

events.title: English Conversation Club
events.description: Are you looking to improve your English? Join our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club at Almaden to practice speaking. Two leaders will guide the group in weekly topics. Basic understanding of English required. The purpose of this group is to practice speaking and to increase a learner's facility and comfort in speaking.
events.blurb: Practice spoken English on weekly topics with two group leaders at Almaden's Conversation Club.

events.title: Monthly Chat with Mayor Moore
events.description: Get ready to talk about what matters most to you. Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.

events.title: Cupertino Fall Bike Fest
events.description: Strap on a helmet and bike to Civic Center Plaza to start the fall with some bike-themed fun! The event will feature bike rides, on-bike and off-bike games, arts and crafts, food and beverages for sale, and much more! Check out the Bike Fest website for the schedule, list of events, and registration form: www.cupertino.gov/bikefest
events.blurb: Bike to Civic Center Plaza for group rides, on-bike games, crafts, and food trucks at the Fall Bike Fest.

events.title: Jewelry Making for Adults
events.description: Get crafty and relax at a jewelry-making night just for adults.. Supplies will be available to create whatever you like. Make something for yourself or a gift for a friend. Better yet, bring a friend! Not sure where to start? We'll have project ideas and examples to help you get inspired. Come be creative, unwind, and have fun.

events.title: In-Person English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: The Edenvale Branch Library presents an in person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. This is a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners who want to develop and increase English Language and vocabulary skills. Participants will be practicing a variety of literacy activities. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice spoken English and build vocabulary with fellow adult learners in a welcoming conversation group.

events.title: Friday Fun: DIY Paper Spinner Craft
events.description: Come make a DIY spinner toy! These spinner toys are so bright and colorful, and they're so cool to play with! Watch the colors combine as the string spinner whirls through the air! ALL supplies are provided! Free. No registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Pearl Avenue Friends of the Library.
events.blurb: Make a DIY paper spinner toy and watch the colors blend as it whirls through the air.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Fulfilling Long Term Goals
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a series workshop on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada walk through strategies for reaching your long term financial goals.

events.title: Insiders: Activities
events.description: Join us for socializing, finding new friends, networking, making jokes, learn to play Dungeons & Dragons, and having fun with art! Insiders programs are geared towards teens and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Caregivers are welcome to join. Snacks will be provided. Walk-ins are welcome!
events.blurb: Socialize, make jokes, try Dungeons & Dragons, and create art with fellow teens and adults in this welcoming group.

events.title: Tai Chi for Seniors
events.description: Join us at Tully library every Thursday for an hour of Tai Chi exercises. Tai Chi improves strength, flexibility, aerobic conditioning, and balance. It's been proven to improve cardiovascular fitness, lower blood pressure, prevent falls, and help people who have arthritis. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Move through an hour of Tai Chi exercises built to boost balance, flexibility, and cardiovascular fitness.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Daniel Kraus
events.description: Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us online as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik. Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as niks, has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fma plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue. The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, andmost lethal of alla rugged, Non Modded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter. The Sickness itself is mutating, possibly even pregnant. And the secret of Fm is more horrific than anyone could have imagined. To survive, Sisilla will need to forsake her predetermined fate and embrace the unknown. About the Author: Daniel Kraus is a Pulitzer Prize-winning, New York Times bestselling writer of novels, TV, and film. His novel Angel Down was the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winner, a New York Times Top 10 Book of 2025, and a national bestseller. His novel Whalefall received a front-cover review in the New York Times Book Review, won the Alex Award, was an L. A. Times Book Prize Finalist, and was a Best Book of 2023 from NPR, the New York Times, Amazon, Chicago Tribune, and more. With Guillermo del Toro, he co-authored The Shape of Water, based on the same idea the two created for the Oscar-winning film. Also with del Toro, Kraus co-authored Trollhunters, which was adapted into the Emmy-winning Netflix series. He co-wrote The Living Dead and Pay the Piper with legendary filmmaker George A. Romero. Krauss The Death and Life of Zebulon Finch was named one of Entertainment Weekly s Top 10 Books of the Year. Kraus has won the Bram Stoker Award, Scribe Award, two Odyssey Awards (for both Rotters and Scowler ), and has appeared multiple times as Library Guild selections, and more. Krauss work has been translated into over 25 languages. He lives with his partner in Chicago. Visit him at danielkraus.com.
events.blurb: Hear author Daniel Kraus discuss his new novel The Sixth Nik in an online talk.

events.title: San Francisco Opera Guild: Simon Boccanegra preview
events.description: Join us for a preview and 90-minute presentation by Professor Mary Ann Smart of the San Francisco Opera's upcoming performance of Simon Boccanegra by Giuseppe Verdi Simon Boccanegra accepts the candidacy to lead the new Republic of Genoa with the hopes of uniting his family. But on the very day he is elected Doge, tragedy strikes—his beloved dies, and his infant daughter vanishes. Over a decade later, he must navigate dangerous politics and newfound family, set to some of the most beautiful music Verdi ever composed. Mary Ann Smart is the Gladyce Arata Terrill Endowed Chair and a professor in the Department of Music at the University of California, Berkeley. Much of her research has focused on social dimensions of opera in nineteenth-century Europe. Her first book, Mimomania: Music and Gesture in Nineteenth-Century Opera (2004), drew on textual sources (treatises on acting, staging manuals) and musical evidence to suggest close ties between musical patterns and physical gesture in repertory stretching from the first French grand operas of the 1830s to Verdi's Aida and Wagner's Ring. Her second book, Waiting for Verdi: Opera and Political Opinion in Nineteenth-Century Italy, 1815–1848 (2018), tackled the fraught question of how opera mattered to audiences in nineteenth-century Italy, and how it made a difference to political and social realities during that period. She has also co-edited books and journal issues on gender and sexuality in opera, nineteenth-century patterns of reception of French grand opera, and (with Nicholas Mathew) on musicology's romance with "quirk historicism." She has published articles on the lives and public images of nineteenth-century female singers, on the ways madness is depicted in opera, and on recent and contemporary staging of canonical opera. She is currently working on two book-length projects—a theoretical study of trends in opera production since 1970 and an alternative history of French theories of voice, music, and language in the twentieth century, extending from Proust through the speech archive of Ferdinand Brunot, Michel Leiris's flamboyantly operatic memoirs, cabaret songs based on the poetry of Raymond Queneau, and the austere audiovisual experiments of Alain Resnais. Registration is not required, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before. Future opera previews are scheduled for September 15, October 6 and May 26.

events.title: San Francisco Opera Guild: Mary, Queen of Scots preview
events.description: Join us for a 90-minute preview and presentation by Laura Stanfield Prichard about Thea Musgrave's Mary, Queen of Scots. At 18 years old, Mary is poised, politically savvy, and confident in her divine claim to the Scottish throne. However, the Scotland she returns to bears little resemblance to the country she left behind as a child. Mary must outmaneuver her power-hungry male advisors to hold on to her throne. In Mary, Queen of Scots, composer Thea Musgrave brings one of history's most captivating figures to the stage with a score as bold and compelling as its heroine. As Mary navigates a treacherous political landscape, she leans on her closest advisors: her calculating half-brother James, Earl of Moray; the enigmatic Earl of Bothwell; and her charming, but weak-willed future husband, Lord Darnley. Slowly, but surely, each man's hunger for her power reveals itself in increasingly manipulative ways, and Mary must outmaneuver one betrayal after the next. Making her company debut, Clelia Cafiero conducts this co-production with English National Opera by director/designer Stewart Laing sets 16th-century intrigue against a backdrop of contemporary Scottish life and sectarian violence, lending fresh resonance to an almost 500-year-old story. Laura Stanfield Prichard studied at Yale, Emory, and the University of Illinois; she holds master's and doctoral degrees in choral conducting, library science, musicology, and education. She lectures regularly for the San Francisco and Chicago Symphonies and opera companies in Boston and San Francisco (since 1995). The Boston Musical Intelligencer sent her to Cuba in 2015 as a foreign correspondent, and she has reviewed concerts for them since 2010. She was the President of the Pacific Chapter of the College Music Society (1996-98) and Assistant Conductor of the San Francisco Symphony Chorus under Vance George (1995-2003). She and her husband Michael sing with the Boston and San Francisco Symphony Choruses. Her twenty-five continuous years of college teaching have focused on interdisciplinary cultural analysis of music, dance, and art history. Recent publications include editorial prefaces for orchestral scores (Musikproduktion Höflich, Munich, Germany), 650 translations of song and choral texts ( www.lieder.net ), and more than three dozen entries to the Encyclopedia of Latin American Popular Music (2012), the landmark revision of the multi-volume New Grove Dictionary of American Music (2013), the Sage International Encyclopedia of Music and Culture (2019), and the forthcoming Music Around the World (2020). She was a finalist for the 2015 Pauline Alderman Award for outstanding writing on women and music and the 2019 Kurt Weill Award for writing on contemporary musical theater. Registration is not required but you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Hear Laura Stanfield Prichard preview Thea Musgrave's opera Mary, Queen of Scots at the Art Center Auditorium.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Priya Parker
events.description: Join us for a paradigm-shifting, essential event as we sit down with world-renowned master facilitator Priya Parker to discuss her groundbreaking new book, The Art of Fighting: The Transformative Power of Conflict. In The Art of Fighting, Priya Parker explains that we can't form and grow effective relationships without a fight. She rejects the idea that conflict is abnormal or that good groups don't fight. All groups change and evolve; indeed, its because people disagree that good groups flourish. As she did in the now-classic The Art of Gathering, Parker draws on her far-reaching experience as a conflict facilitator, her own detailed research, and real-world examples to lay out the ways that people can identify disputes, determine how to address them, and what to do if they are insurmountable. Whether people disagree in the boardroom or the locker room, on a playground or in church, online or in person, conflict is a part of life, and understanding healthy conflict and how to harness its power is more important than ever. The Art of Fighting is a vital primer to help all of us understand how to do that. About the Author: Priya Parker is an internationally recognized expert on creating purposeful gatherings and reimagining how we come together in our communities and our workplaces. She is a conflict facilitator, strategic advisor, speaker, and author of the acclaimed book The Art of Gathering: How We Meet and Why it Matters and the host of The Art of Gathering Digital Course. Whether addressing CEOs, non-profit leaders, students or community organizers, Parker captivates audiences with her unique blend of storytelling, research-backed insights, and practical strategies.
events.blurb: Hear facilitator Priya Parker discuss her new book The Art of Fighting in an online author talk.

events.title: When the Tiger Smoked a Pipe: The Art of Korea
events.description: Registration is required. Sign up below to receive the Zoom information on the morning of the event. Often heard at the beginning of Korean legends and folktales, When the tiger smoked a pipe is a familiar phrase akin to Once upon a time. This program draws from the Asian Art Museums collection of Korean art to explore a layered and transformative history of artmaking. Renowned for its ceramics and textiles, Korea has also created, adapted, and refined a variety of art forms. Today, Korea is among the leaders of contemporary art production. Presented by the Asian Art Museum. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Learn about Korean legends and folk art in this online talk drawing from the Asian Art Museum.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Lucky Diaz
events.description: Grab a pocketful of change and get ready to dance down the street! Join us for an energetic conversation as we celebrate the joy of community and summer fun with Latin Grammy-winning musician Lucky Diaz, author of the sensational bilingual picture book, Paletero Man. Whats the best way to cool off on a hot summer day? Run quick and find Paletero Jos! Follow along with our narrator as he passes through his busy neighborhood in search of the Paletero Man. But when he finally catches up with him, our narrators pockets are empty. Oh no! What happened to his dinero? It will take the help of the entire community to get the tasty treat now. Inspired by the vibrant rhythms of Los Angeles and Diazs own hit song, this beautiful story invites readers into a sun-drenched neighborhood where the ring of a bell means the best treat of the day is just around the corner. About the Author: Lucky Diaz is a Grammy Award-winning, multi Latin Grammy Award-winning artist, acclaimed author, and a leading voice in contemporary children's literature. A six-time Emmy-nominated songwriter and Berklee College of Music alumnus, Diaz made history as the first North American children's artist to win a Latin Grammy. His work bridges music and storytelling, creating a distinct body of bilingual work rooted in the cultural life of Mexican American communities in Los Angeles. As an author, Diaz has earned some of the highest honors in publishing. His books have received starred reviews from Kirkus Reviews, School Library Journal, Publishers Weekly, and Booklist, placing him among a rare group of creators recognized across every major literary journal. His breakout title Paletero Man received a Kirkus star and audiobook distinction and was awarded the 2024 Alma Flor Ada Award for its lasting contribution to Latino-centered storytelling. He is also a recipient of the Parents Choice Gold Award and a Nappa Award, further recognizing his impact on family audiences. His latest book, Fix-It Familia, continues to build national recognition, with a Spanish edition arriving this summer, expanding access to bilingual readers and classrooms across the country. Diazs work has been featured and praised by NPR, Billboard, The New York Times, and People Magazine, positioning him as a trusted creative voice at the intersection of culture, music, and literature. Through his books, recordings, and performances with Lucky Diaz and the Family Jam Band, Diaz continues to expand the possibilities of American storytelling. He is not only contributing to the field, he is helping define it.
events.blurb: Hear Latin Grammy-winning musician Lucky Diaz talk about his bilingual picture book Paletero Man online.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Veronica Roth
events.description: A single choice can transform your destiny. Join us for an online conversation with #1 New York Times bestselling author Veronica Roth as we celebrate the enduring legacy of her Divergent series, one of the most iconic young adult series of a generation, and get an exclusive sneak peek into her highly anticipated upcoming novel, The Sixth Faction! Fifteen years after readers first stepped into dystopian Chicago alongside Tris Prior, the Divergent universe continues to captivate readers with its unflinching exploration of identity, courage, and sacrifice. And in the alternate universe of The Sixth Faction, we revisit familiar characters in a completely new way… Beatrice Prior stands on the brink of a decision every person in her world must make: five factions, five futures, five lives. She has a plan: shes going to make the bravest choice and leave Abnegation to join Dauntless, even though it means abandoning her family. But when tragedy strikes at her choosing ceremony, everything changesher world, her plans, even Beatrice herself. Her decision will thrust her into the crosshairs of an underground rebellion, where a boy with secrets as dangerous as her owna boy with only a number for a namemay be the only person she can trust. One choice will change everything. About the Author: Veronica Roth is the #1 New York Times best-selling author of numerous titles including When Among Crows, Chosen Ones, the Divergent series, Carve the Mark and the upcoming Seek the Traitors Son. Veronica lives with her husband and their dog in Chicago, a city that she lovingly features (and frequently destroys) in many of her novels.
events.blurb: Hear Veronica Roth talk about the Divergent series and get a preview of what's next for her.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Carolyn Russo
events.description: Join us for a captivating online conversation with acclaimed author and Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo as we dive into her fascinating book, The Ascent of Rauschenberg. Explore the towering legacy, unexpected inspirations, and creative heights of one of America's most influential artistic icons. Most famous for his groundbreaking Combinespainting and sculpture hybrids that often incorporated everyday objects American artist Robert Rauschenberg (1925-2008) created within a range of mediums, including collage, performance, photography, and printmaking. But a connective tissue through it all was his fascination with flight. The Ascent of Rauschenberg explores the flight motif across his work, spanning birds, insects, aviation, spaceflight, sensory experiences, and metaphors for his own life. More than 150 images reveal the vibrant scope of his work, from lithographs inspired by the Apollo 11 launch that NASA invited him to witness and document, to a Combine featuring a taxidermied eagle that evokes Roman mythology. Nine accompanying essays reflect on his many flight themes and subtleties that might otherwise be overlooked. The book also includes archival photographs and personal papers from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation. About the Author: Carolyn Russo is curator of the art collection at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. She has lectured internationally on the subject of art and flight and is the author of several publications including The Ascent of Rauschenberg: Reinventing the Art of Flight, Art of the Airport Tower, In Plane View: Abstractions of Flight, and Women and Flight: Portraits of Contemporary Women Pilots.
events.blurb: Hear Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo discuss her book on Robert Rauschenberg's art and life.

events.title: Concert: Music at Kohl Mansion presents Escher String Quartet
events.description: Now in our fourth year of partnership with Music at Kohl Mansion, we proudly present the Escher String Quartet. The Escher String Quartet has established itself as one of the most accomplished chamber ensembles of its generation. Formed in New York City in 2005, and named after the Dutch graphic artist M. C. Escher, the quartet is celebrated for performances that combine technical brilliance, interpretive insight, and a distinctive ensemble sound. The group serves as Artists of the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center and has earned international recognition for its commitment to both the core string quartet repertoire and contemporary music. The quartet has appeared at many of the world's leading concert halls and festivals, including London's Wigmore Hall, Amsterdam's Concertgebouw, the Kennedy Center, Paris's Auditorium du Louvre, and major chamber music festivals throughout North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia. Praised by critics for their precision, warmth, and expressive depth, the Escher String Quartet has received numerous honors, including the prestigious Avery Fisher Career Grant and Lincoln Center's Martin E. Segal Award. The ensemble's critically acclaimed recording projects include the complete string quartets of Alexander Zemlinsky and Felix Mendelssohn and more. Through its adventurous programming and consistently compelling performances, the Escher String Quartet continues to be recognized as one of the leading chamber ensembles on the international stage.
events.blurb: Hear the Escher String Quartet perform chamber music as part of Music at Kohl Mansion's season.

events.title: Am I Being Tracked?: A Guide to Digital Privacy
events.description: Registration is required. Sign up below to receive the Zoom information on the morning of the event. Every click, search, and scroll leaves a trail but how much of your life is actually being monitored, and by whom? In Am I Being Tracked?, we take a hype-free look at the modern tracking ecosystem. First, well debunk some myths around online privacy. Next, well reframe how you think about digital privacy, shifting the goal from total invisibility to smart data management. Finally, you'll get a practical checklist of steps you can take right now to gain control over your personal data. About the Presenter: Iman Saleh is a local Mountain View mom and a privacy professional with more than 24 years of experience in big tech and academia. She holds a Ph D in Software Engineering and is recognized as a Fellow of Information Privacy by the International Association of Privacy Professionals (Iapp).
events.blurb: Learn how your online activity gets tracked and what you can do to guard your digital privacy.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Cherie Dimaline
events.description: Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Mtis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls. Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumorand accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimalines expansive literary careerfrom the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and Ven Co. About the Author: Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by Time magazine, one of the Best Ya Books of All Time and won the Governor Generals Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel Venco debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (Aila Honor Book, Aura Award winner, Crime Writers Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor Generals Award Finalist). Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Mtis Community and has written and produced for Marvel, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.

events.description: Together with our friends at Deer Hollow Farm, our librarians will present a spooky-themed storytime at the farm with books, songs, and rhymes. We will also get to meet some of the farm animals up close! Meet us there: Deer Hollow Farm, 22500 Cristo Rey Dr., Cupertino Please note: the parking lot for Deer Hollow Farm is about a one-mile flat, paved walk to the farm. We recommend walking shoes, hats, and/or strollers. Also, there will be limited seating-- prepare to sit on the floor if you can.

events.blurb: Hear a spooky-themed storytime with books, songs, and rhymes, then meet farm animals up close.

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident Register
events.blurb: Walk Stevens Creek with a naturalist, identify aquatic insects, and learn the steelhead's life cycle.

events.title: Drop-in Bike Clinic
events.venue: Bike Fix-it Station (Outside Franklin St. Entrance)
events.description: Come join us every third Saturday of the month for the Drop-in Bike Clinic! Use our tools to work on your bike. All ages welcome. Professional bike mechanic Ryan Murphy will be available for advice and help with: Changing a tire Adjusting gears and brakes Identifying that mysterious noise, and more! Meet at our Dero Fix-it station, on Franklin Street. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Bring your bike and use the tools on hand while mechanic Ryan Murphy offers repair advice.

events.title: NUMU Youth Still Life: Spooky Skeleton Figure Drawing (Ages 7-16)
events.description: Meet us at the New Museum Los Gatos, where the staff will arrange a (fake decor) skeleton and a (decor) dog skeleton along with a few spooky objects from our collection for children ages 7-16 to sketch on black or gray paper with white drawing pencils. This event is a young artist's dream as it will take place in the Museum's professional studio setting! All materials are provided. Registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event.
events.blurb: Sketch a decorated skeleton and spooky museum objects in white pencil on dark paper at NUMU.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird Id and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shoulder Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident Register
events.blurb: Join a ranger-led hike to spot and identify riparian birds like hawks and owls along the trail.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming of age story revealing the truth behind the fairytale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this acapella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Catch this Emmy writer's drama on the woman who inspired Alice in Wonderland.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Teen Movie Night - Jurassic Park (1993)
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 N Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: Cupertino teens, get ready for movie night! Join us at the Quinlan Community Center on Friday, September 25 for a free screening of Jurassic Park on the big screen. Bring your friends, grab some free food and snacks, and enjoy the movie together. Doors open at 6 p.m., movie starts at 6:30 p.m. Admission is free, but please Rsvp so we can plan for enough food. Rsvp at cupertino.gov/teenmovienight.
events.blurb: Watch Jurassic Park on the big screen with fellow teens and free snacks at Quinlan Community Center.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.

events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: IDs for the Trees
events.description: Explore Mc Clellan Ranch Preserve alongside one of our Park Rangers. You'll learn how to use a dichotomous key to identify the different trees of the area and their uses. All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident Register
events.blurb: Walk a quarter-mile trail with a Park Ranger learning to identify trees using a dichotomous key.

events.title: 2026 Cupertino Community Service Awards
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 N. Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: The third annual Cupertino Community Service Awards will take place on Wednesday, October 28. This ceremony will recognize the 2026 Crest Awards (Cupertino Recognizes Extra Steps Taken), and Commissioners who served on a City Commission. Doors open at 5:30 p.m., program starts at 6 p.m. Rsvp is required, registration will open for the public on Monday, September 21.
events.blurb: See Cupertino honor Crest Award winners and city commissioners at this evening recognition ceremony.

events.title: Na Leo Mokupuni in Cupertino
events.description: Na Leo Mokupuni in Cupertino – meaning island sounds in Cupertino Experience the rhythms, songs, and dances of the islands! Na Leo Mokupuni brings together performers to celebrate the vibrant traditions of island music and dance—right here in Cupertino. Preregistration is recommended. Limited tickets available at the door, while supplies last.
events.blurb: Watch performers share island songs and dances at this Hawaiian-style community celebration.

events.title: Breakfast with Santa
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: You and your family are invited to a festive breakfast celebration with Santa! Enjoy delicious North Pole pancakes prepared by Santa's elves, take photos with Santa, and explore a holiday workshop filled with crafts and activities for children. Three seatings: 8:30 a.m., 9:30 a.m., 10:30 a.m. Register Registration opens in late July.
events.blurb: Eat Santa's North Pole pancakes, snap photos with the man himself, and try holiday crafts with the kids.

events.title: Monster Mash
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Get ready for a fang-tastic good time at Cupertino Parks and Recreation's annual Monster Mash Halloween event at the Quinlan Community Center. Put on your favorite costume and enjoy an evening of games, trick-or-treating, spooky crafts, and pumpkin decorating. It's a fun-filled night of Halloween activities for the whole family.
events.blurb: Wear a costume and join games, trick-or-treating, and pumpkin decorating at this Halloween party.
